completed_items.title: Move the rate-limit gate ahead of the observer
completed_items.what_changed: Both rate-limit gates (the in-memory publishBlockedUntil check and the STAB-001 60-minute publisherHistory gatekeeper) were extracted into lib/publisher/cooldownGate.ts and are now invoked immediately after the maintenance pre-flight, before `log = await observe()` in lib/publisher/publisherRun.ts. The 60-minute window became PUBLISH_COOLDOWN_WINDOW_MS in lib/publisher/constants.ts.
completed_items.why_a_new_file: publisherRun.ts hit 511 lines after the in-place block move and `npm run lint:structure` failed on the 500-line size budget. Extraction was the fix, not an unprompted refactor.
completed_items.behavior_change: The `rate_limited` result no longer carries gapInfo. There is no observer log at that point. Verified by grep that the only gapInfo consumers are lib/scheduler/run.ts:173/176/202, none of which read it on the rate_limited path.
completed_items.test_seam_added: runPublisher(force, overrides) gained an optional second argument, `{ runObserver }`. Node is v20.20.2 here and `mock.module` requires Node 22.3+, so an injected seam was the only way to satisfy the spec's 'asserted by spy, not by log inspection' requirement.
completed_items.verified_by: bash scripts/run-tests.sh tests/unit/publisherCooldown.test.ts - the guard asserts observerCalls === 0 and decision === 'rate_limited'.

completed_items.title: Split success out of the gap_skip scheduling branch
completed_items.what_changed: The SchedulerTickOutcome 'success' variant carries a new `cooldownApplies` boolean. A `published_verified` result now schedules PUBLISH_COOLDOWN_WINDOW_MINUTES + 1 (61 minutes) under reason 'post_publish_cooldown'. lib/scheduler/run.ts imports the constant from lib/publisher/index.js so the gate and the schedule cannot drift.
completed_items.deviation_from_spec: The spec said 'give success its own branch'. dry_run also maps to the success outcome, but lib/publisher/history.ts:104 shows getLastSuccessfulPublish only matches decision === 'published_verified', so a dry run starts no cooldown. Making dry_run wait 61 minutes would have been an unrequested behavior regression for a debugging mode, so dry_run stays on gapRecheckIntervalMinutes. Guarded by a test.
completed_items.verified_by: Two tests in tests/unit/schedulerStabilization.test.ts: verified publish schedules >60 and <=61 minutes; dry run schedules >2 and <=3 minutes.

completed_items.title: Make an active block deadline non-shortenable
completed_items.what_changed: scheduleNext() in lib/scheduler/run.ts now reads publishBlockedUntil and maintenanceBlockedUntil via getPublisherControls() from lib/state/index.js, and clamps the computed deadline to the later of the two when either exceeds it. The losing schedule is logged with status:'clamped', clampedBy, discardedReason and discardedMinutes. The setTimeout delay is computed from the clamped deadline, not from nextMinutes.
completed_items.deviation_from_spec: The spec said max(now + nextMinutes, blockUntil). The implementation uses blockUntil + 60s, matching the 1-minute buffer the existing rate_limited branch already applies. A clamp to the exact boundary would fire a tick at the instant the block expires and risk bouncing straight back into rate_limited.
completed_items.verified_by: tests/unit/schedulerStabilization.test.ts - with publishBlockedUntil 45 minutes out, scheduler.setControls({ baseIntervalMinutes: 5 }) leaves nextTickEta at or after the block deadline and no earlier than before the call.

completed_items.title: Give the concurrency skip its own decision
completed_items.what_changed: 'already_running' added to PublisherRunDecision in contracts/models.ts and to PUBLISHER_DECISIONS in lib/publisher/constants.ts (which also picked up the system_maintenance entry it was missing). The guard in runPublisher() returns it instead of 'publisher_error'. lib/scheduler/run.ts adds an { type: 'already_running' } outcome that schedules a 1-minute retry and does not touch consecutiveFailures. lib/analytics/schedulerSignals.ts classifies it non_adaptive alongside observer_error / manual_override_disabled / rate_limited / system_maintenance.
completed_items.side_effect_checked: lib/aiAdvisor.ts:157 counts failures as decision === 'publisher_error' || 'observer_error', so it now correctly ignores overlaps. No other consumer of the decision string exists in routes/ or src/ (grep, no hits).
completed_items.verified_by: Two tests: publisherCooldown.test.ts asserts an overlapping runPublisher returns 'already_running'; schedulerStabilization.test.ts asserts consecutiveFailures stays 0 and the next tick is <= 1 minute.

completed_items.title: Replace the tautological cooldown tests with real gate coverage
completed_items.what_changed: The two tests at the former tests/unit/publisherCooldown.test.ts:49-70 were deleted. They re-implemented the cooldown arithmetic in the test body and asserted against themselves. Four real guards replaced them, each landed in the same commit as the item it guards, per the spec's execution_mode.
completed_items.note: RTG-005 has no separate commit by design - the spec required each work item to land with its regression test, so batching the tests into a fifth commit would have contradicted RTG-001's own instruction.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The run log after a verified publish shows one publish followed by one long wait, with no rate_limited entry three minutes later.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The code path is covered by a unit test asserting a ~61-minute schedule, but no production run has occurred. This is the criterion the one-day soak below is for.
